title: RaceLab — give the repair a test it can fail
disclosures: Actual Edge interaction clips and stills with editorial crops, original graphic framing and synthesized sound bed; preparation omitted
Scenes 1-5 retain Muse Spark study evidence; scenes 6-8 capture one new live Muse Spark 1.3 investigation on the public Cloudflare MVP; model waiting omitted
Generic Xiaomi MiMo TTS Mia voice, no voice cloning; separate MiMo ASR checks; captions use measured speech-beat boundaries rather than provider word timestamps
Real disposable SQLite and finite controlled process sequences; no whole-application or external delivery guarantee
New film integration is separate from frozen comparison studies and failed recording attempts; no general repair-rate or human-impact claim
Tang Vu built RaceLab during the event; TEND and earlier event infrastructure are pre-existing inputs

scenes.chapter: A passing test. A missing job.
scenes.heading:
It passed.
Then the worker died.
beats: Your tests pass. Then a worker dies, and a job never comes back.
Race Lab reproduces the failure and checks a Meta-generated repair.
Built by Tang Vu during this hackathon, using earlier TEND source and event infrastructure.
scenes.narration: Your tests pass. Then a worker dies, and a job never comes back. Race Lab reproduces the failure and checks a Meta-generated repair. Built by Tang Vu during this hackathon, using earlier TEND source and event infrastructure.

scenes.heading:
A process stops.
The database stays.
scenes.metricLabel: the claim persists after the worker exits
beats: This is a real TypeScript method from a pinned public repository.
It runs against a real, disposable database, inside a separate worker process.
Claim the job. Commit the row. Stop the worker.
The database survives. The original method leaves the job claimed.

scenes.heading:
Watch the state.
Find the missing recovery.
beats: Now start a replacement worker on the same database.
The trace shows exactly what committed, and when the old process exited.
The original misses the claimed row.
The repair reclaims it after the declared sixty-second lease, without changing its payload.

scenes.heading:
A hypothesis. A probe.
A repair that must run.
beats: Meta's model sees the source and the contract, then chooses a crash probe.
The tool returns an actual failure.
Next, Meta writes a candidate method; independent code executes and scores it.
Open the hypothesis, feedback and diff. The model never awards itself a pass.

scenes.heading:
Recover the job.
Respect the owner.
scenes.metricLabel: conditions / each of two feedback lifecycle candidates
beats: But recovering one job is only half the story.
A worker may still be alive. Or it may return with an old token.
The lifecycle adapter tests contention, interruption, renewal and stale ownership.
Both feedback candidates pass all ten conditions, with guards inside their source.

scenes.chapter: Bring a method. Run Muse Spark.
scenes.heading:
Your method.
A new Muse repair.

Import this file. Its thirty-second lease can steal a live worker’s job.
Muse Spark investigates the new input, receives executed feedback, and writes a new repair.
